requirements.evidence: Contract present: enum CallMode (app/Enums/CallMode.php:5-10), NoWaitingTicketsException extends RuntimeException (app/Exceptions/NoWaitingTicketsException.php:7), action signature matches (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:19). Queue row locked and is_active read from DB (CallNextTicket.php:24-27); ordering priority desc/issued_at/id (:69) and normal-only oldest-first (:67); fairness via last 3 by called_at desc, id desc (:33-50); NoWaitingTicketsException when empty (:76-78). Weaknesses: fairness history filters `->where('status', TicketStatus::Called)` (:35) so tickets that later moved past 'called' drop out of the history instead of using called_at; retry loop rethrows LogicException after 5 attempts (:87-89) instead of continuing to skip; return relies on unverified claim that Ticket::call refreshes the model (:83); `#[Transactional]` attribute from `Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Attributes\Transactional` (:13,:18) is very likely a non-existent class.

conventions.evidence: Action placed correctly in app/Actions. But no tests at all despite 'No production code without a test'; imports unsorted (`use LogicException;` before `use Illuminate\...Transactional; use App\Enums\TicketStatus;`, CallNextTicket.php:12-14) which would fail Pint's ordered_imports; no CHANGELOG entry and no PHPDoc on the public __invoke; docs updates (docs/architecture.md:103, docs/business-rules.md:133-136) are one-paragraph summaries that don't describe the ordering, fairness or locking implementation.

security.evidence: Authorization is explicitly out of scope; no user input or mass assignment introduced; queue state read under lockForUpdate (CallNextTicket.php:24). Catching broad LogicException (:85) could mask unrelated logic errors but is not exploitable.

tests.evidence: The diff contains no test files; none of ordering, fairness, modes, inactive queue, empty queue or concurrency re-check is tested.

simplicity.evidence: Reuses Ticket::call (:82) and builds one query. But wraps DB::transaction plus a bogus #[Transactional] attribute (:18,:22), arbitrary 5-attempt counter (:73-90), and duplicated `$mode === CallMode::NormalOnly || $applyNormalOnly` condition (:61,:66).

readability.evidence: Single 80-line closure with step comments; mostly clear names. Misleading comments ('Delegate to Ticket::call which enforces membership', 'ticket is refreshed inside Ticket::call', :82-83) and a dead/meaningless attribute; unsorted imports.

scope.evidence: Only the action, enum, exception and the two requested docs are touched; nothing unrelated.

issues.explanation: No Pest tests ship with the new action, violating the project's mandatory test-first rule and leaving ordering, fairness, modes and failure paths unverified.

Fairness history only considers tickets whose current status is 'called', so tickets that later moved to another status are excluded and the streak of the last 3 calls (by called_at) can be computed wrongly; whereNotNull('called_at') would match the rule.
`#[Transactional]` references `Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Attributes\Transactional`, which is very likely not a real framework class; it is redundant with DB::transaction and misleading.
On a concurrently called candidate the loop gives up and rethrows after 5 attempts instead of skipping to the next ticket, and catching every LogicException can mask unrelated errors.
The returned model's updated status/called_at depends on an unverified assumption that Ticket::call refreshes the instance; no test confirms it.
Docs only state that the action exists; they do not describe ordering, fairness, locking or modes as the task asks, and CHANGELOG.md is not updated.
Imports are not alphabetically ordered, which Pint's Laravel preset would flag.
The normal-only condition is computed twice; a single `$normalOnly` flag would be simpler.

review.summary: The change adds CallMode, NoWaitingTicketsException and a CallNextTicket action that locks the queue, applies modes, ordering and a fairness rule, and delegates the write to Ticket::call, with brief doc notes. The core logic is mostly right, but it ships with no tests, the fairness history filters by current status instead of called_at, it uses a likely non-existent #[Transactional] attribute, and the docs are thin, so it needs changes before merging.
